title: BE(A)WARE - A Booklet on Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds (press release)
notes: RBI press release launching the BE(A)WARE booklet, which covers SIM swaps, phishing/vishing links, lottery frauds and fake loan websites/apps. RBI says customers sharing confidential information, knowingly or unknowingly, is a major cause of fraud. The booklet PDF itself (rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/content/pdfs/BEAWARE07032022.pdf) was behind a bot check and could not be opened.

title: Consumer Awareness - Cyber Threats and Frauds (Press Release 2021-2022/1630)
notes: RBI lists vishing (posing as bank/e-wallet/telecom staff on KYC, unblocking, refund pretexts), phishing links, remote-access apps installed on the victim's device, misuse of UPI collect requests where victims are asked to enter their UPI PIN and end up paying instead of receiving, and fake helpline numbers on search engines and social media.

title: NPCI to tighten UPI rules: Peer-to-peer collect feature to end in October
notes: Reports an NPCI circular dated 29 July 2025 directing that from 1 October 2025 UPI P2P collect requests shall not be processed; merchant collect requests continue. Earlier P2P collect had been capped at Rs 2,000 per transaction; the feature had been misused to trick users into approving payments.

title: UPI Safety Shield
notes: NPCI safety page (JavaScript-rendered; WebFetch returned only the title). Search snippet states UPI PIN is needed only to deduct money and is not required for receiving money, and to scan QR codes only when making a payment.

title: Cyber Crimes - OLX fraud
notes: Describes fraudsters posing as Army/paramilitary personnel buying items on OLX/Quikr, sending a fake payment screenshot, then a QR code and guiding the seller to enter the UPI PIN; each scan debits the seller and the fraudster sends a QR for double the amount to 'fix' it. Advises not to scan a QR code to receive money and to treat urgency and ID cards as warning signs.

title: Raju and The Forty Thieves (RBI Kehta Hai)
notes: RBI pictorial booklet and videos on fraud modus operandi; page redirected bots to the RBI home page. Search snippet lists entries including QR code scams, illegal loan apps, fraudsters posing as recovery agents, social welfare scheme fraud and online job fraud.

title: NPCI warns users of call merging scam targeting OTPs
notes: Reports NPCI's X (Twitter) warning that scammers use call merging to obtain OTPs: a caller posing as an event organiser or job interviewer claims a mutual friend shared the number and asks the victim to merge a call that is actually the bank's OTP verification call. NPCI advises not merging calls with unknown numbers, notes banks never ask for OTPs on calls, and says to report to 1930.

title: Cyber Byte (English) March 2025
publisher: Communication & IT Directorate, Central Reserve Police Force (MHA)
notes: CRPF newsletter summarising NPCI's call-merging warning (caller says he got your number from a friend, merges a genuine bank OTP call), a government alert on 'pig butchering'/investment scams targeting unemployed youth, students and housewives that can lead to cyber slavery (citing the MHA annual report), and the SpyLend Android loan-app malware enabling extortion of Indian users.

title: eSIM scam is targeting users in India: Here's how it happens and how to stay safe
notes: Citing I4C, describes fake eSIM activation calls and links that appear to come from the telecom operator; after the victim clicks, the physical SIM goes dead and calls, SMS and OTPs move to the attacker, who resets passwords and approves UPI payments. Mentions an I4C-reported victim who lost Rs 4 lakh.

title: SIM swap, eSIM scams: How scammers can steal your phone number
notes: Reports I4C's warning on eSIM/SIM-swap fraud: impersonators of telecom staff or officials send fake activation links or urgent SIM-swap requests; red flags include sudden loss of signal and missing OTPs. Says I4C reported DoT had blocked 3 to 4 lakh SIM cards used for fraud and advises asking the operator to freeze the SIM if signal drops unexpectedly.

title: Gurugram police warns against 5G fraud
notes: Gurugram Police reported the city's first 5G-upgrade fraud on 1 Oct 2022: scammers posing as telecom executives send a link and gain access to phones on the pretext of upgrading to 5G. Police advised never sharing OTPs and reporting to 1930.

title: Googling customer care numbers? Be warned of scammers, says Hyd police advisory
notes: Reports a Hyderabad police advisory on fake customer care numbers found via Google and Justdial: a Zomato customer seeking a refund shared bank details and UPI PIN and lost Rs 70,000; an airline customer was asked to pay Rs 75 via Google Pay, then for card details. Police say genuine customer care never asks for card, OTP or UPI PIN details.

title: Fraud Alert: UPI Is Fast & Convenient, but One Careless Tap Can Cost You Dearly
notes: Describes current UPI tricks: QR codes sent on WhatsApp promising a refund or cashback, collect requests saying money is waiting to be collected, fake customer care asking to install remote-access apps or approve UPI requests, fake payment screenshots and tampered shop QR codes. Notes RBI's framework links customer liability to prompt reporting (within three working days).

title: Money transferred by mistake? Fake credit SMS scam (WebQoof decode)
notes: Describes a January 2025 attempt: a caller claiming to be the victim's father's friend said the father asked him to send money via Google Pay; a fake SMS showing Rs 30,000 credited arrived from a personal mobile number, and the caller said he sent 30,000 instead of 3,000 by mistake and asked for the difference back. Advises verifying with the named relative and checking the bank sender ID; reporting via Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi) or 1930.

title: Bengaluru entrepreneur narrowly escapes this SMS scam: how to not fall for this old-school technique
notes: A caller posing as the father's elderly acquaintance said his transfer to the father failed, sent fake credit SMSes (Rs 10,000 then Rs 30,000) from a 10-digit number, claimed he sent Rs 30,000 instead of 3,000 by mistake and asked for Rs 27,000 back urgently, citing a hospital/medical emergency.

title: Rs 70,000 gone in 15 minutes! Indore man falls for fake bank credit SMS scam
notes: A caller who said he knew the victim personally claimed to transfer Rs 25,000, asked him to check his SMS and forward money to another number; fabricated credit SMSes led to seven transfers totalling Rs 70,000. Police registered a case under BNS sections 318(4) and 319(2).

title: NPCI cautions consumers against downloading AnyDesk app
notes: Reports RBI Alert 1/2019 (14 Feb 2019) on fraud using remote screen access apps and NPCI's caution: fraudsters get victims to install AnyDesk, share the 9-digit code and grant permissions, then use the victim's payment and banking apps. NPCI's risk head advised never giving anyone access to your handset through such apps.

title: Google rolls out on-device scam detection in India as digital fraud losses top Rs 70 billion
notes: Google piloted Android alerts with Navi, Paytm and Google Pay that warn users who open financial apps while screen sharing during a call, with options to end the call or stop sharing. Cites an MHA estimate of Rs 70 billion digital-fraud losses in the first five months of 2025.

title: Invited to wedding? Police say check the link before you click
notes: Himachal Pradesh SP (Cybercrime) warns that fake wedding invitations arrive on WhatsApp as APK files or phishing links; the malware steals photos, contacts and banking details and forwards similar invites to the victim's contacts. Police say genuine wedding cards are JPG or PDF files, never APKs; report on 1930.

title: 336 fake APKs linked to Rs 125 crore fraud: Gujarat Police nab Jamtara gang members
notes: Surat City Cyber Crime Cell case: fake APKs posing as bank apps (e.g. a fake PNB One), PM-Kisan, RTO challans, customer support and hospitals were spread via WhatsApp and Telegram; police analysed 336 APKs linked to 5,613 compromised devices and 1,06,643 debit transactions worth about Rs 125.39 crore, with money routed to mule accounts.

title: Fraud Alert: From e-Challan, Gas Bill Updates to APK Traps - How Malware Scams Are Draining Bank Accounts
notes: Reports a CERT-In alert (number and date not stated) on an Android campaign using fake 'RTO Challan.apk', 'MParivahan.apk' and 'Gas Bill Update.apk' files sent via WhatsApp, SMS and Telegram; the malware reads and forwards bank OTPs, requests VPN permission and overlays fake screens on banking/UPI apps. Advises verifying challans only at echallan.parivahan.gov.in.

title: Hyderabad man duped of Rs 1.95 lakh via fake PM Kisan APK
notes: A Yousufguda resident installed a 'PM Kisan' APK received on WhatsApp from an unknown number in late July 2025; his phone was hacked, messages were sent to his contacts and Rs 1.95 lakh was debited. Hyderabad Cybercrime Police registered a case.

title: Govt blocks 100 websites involved in job scams, illegal investments
notes: Reports the MHA statement that I4C's National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit identified 100+ overseas-run websites for task-based part-time job and illegal investment frauds, blocked by MeitY. Modus operandi: Google/Meta ads such as 'Ghar baithe job', a WhatsApp/Telegram agent, like/subscribe or map-rating tasks with small commissions, then larger deposits that get frozen. Targets: retired employees, women and unemployed youth; proceeds moved via mule/rented accounts, cards, crypto and overseas ATMs.

title: Woman loses Rs 32.8 lakh in part-time work scam
notes: Cyberabad Cyber Crime Police case: a WhatsApp offer of Rs 600-1,000 a day for rating restaurants led to a Telegram 'VIP Task Group'; when withdrawals failed the victim was told to pay for 'task repairs', to release a blocked withdrawal, because her 'credit score' was too low, and to open a bigger withdrawal account, totalling Rs 32,82,573 over 47 transactions; small payouts of Rs 53,139 kept her engaged.

title: Curbing Cyber Frauds in Digital India (PIB backgrounder)
publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
notes: Government backgrounder: notes organised fraud linked to 'fraud factories' in Southeast Asia (citing ED), online betting apps that lured users into wallet deposits generating over Rs 400 crore of criminal proceeds, the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act passed 21 Aug 2025 banning online money gaming, over 9.42 lakh SIM cards and 2,63,348 IMEIs blocked, and CFCFRMS/1930 saving over Rs 5,489 crore across 17.82 lakh complaints.

title: Cyber gangs exploit job market, Telangana police warn citizens
notes: Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police (DCP Crime) say 26,809 fake job scam cases were registered in Telangana from January 2024 to August 2025. Scammers harvest data from job portals, hold fake interviews, collect registration, insurance and security deposit fees and send fake offer letters; overseas variants include a New Zealand visa-and-job offer. Police say genuine companies do not ask for money before giving a job.

title: Nearly 7,000 Indians rescued from Cambodia, Myanmar, Laos cybercrime compounds since 2022: Centre
notes: Reports MoS External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh's written reply in Parliament: 6,998 Indians rescued from cybercrime compounds in 2022-2025 (Cambodia 2,533; Laos 2,297; Myanmar 2,168), lured by fake job offers from dubious firms via unscrupulous agents and illegal channels. MEA advises using only government-authorised recruiting agents.

title: Postal Department issues advisory warning about fake job rackets
notes: PIB page returned HTTP 403. Search snippet: India Post warns that fake selection orders are being issued and states it does not ask, solicit or accept any money from applicants.

title: I4C warns investors against fake WhatsApp stock tips, fake trading apps
notes: Reports I4C's July 2026 advisory: fraudsters add people to WhatsApp/Telegram groups with 'VIP stock tips' and guaranteed returns, send fake trading app links that show fabricated profits, and on withdrawal block the account or demand taxes, processing or verification fees. I4C says genuine brokers never require extra deposits to release funds; cites a retired Mumbai scientist who lost Rs 1.3 crore.

title: Advisory Against investment in Fraudulent Trading Schemes claiming to be offered to Indian residents by FPIs (PR No. 53/2025)
publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
notes: SEBI press release (copy hosted by HDFC Mutual Fund) warning about social media, WhatsApp, Telegram and apps offering market access via FPIs/FIIs, with claims of an 'institutional trading account', discounted or guaranteed IPO allotment, anchor book access and discounted block trades. SEBI says the FPI route is unavailable to resident Indians (limited exceptions) and to verify registration on sebi.gov.in.

title: Palghar bank official duped of Rs 46.41 lakh in stock trading fraud
notes: MBVV Police case: victim added to WhatsApp investment groups by people posing as executives of reputed firms, shown a fake SEBI registration certificate and told to install apps via links; the app showed Rs 8.12 crore profit on Rs 46.41 lakh invested, and withdrawal required an extra 10 per cent 'tax'.

title: The Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Bill, 2018 (bill track)
notes: Summarises the BUDS Bill: deposit schemes not registered with a listed regulator are banned; running one carries 2-7 years' imprisonment and Rs 3-10 lakh fine, defaulting 3-10 years and up to twice the amount collected; inducing depositors by falsifying facts is an offence; a Competent Authority can attach property and a Designated Court distributes proceeds; an online database of deposit takers is provided for.

title: Saradha Group financial scandal
notes: Encyclopaedic summary: a group of 200+ companies in eastern India ran a Ponzi-style collective investment scheme mislabelled as a chit fund, selling high-return deposits through commission agents; it collapsed in April 2013 after collecting an estimated Rs 200-300 billion from about 1.7 million depositors, leading to SEBI Act amendments and a CBI probe.

title: MP News: Scammers con elderly man of Rs 9.25 lakh promising high returns
notes: Indore police cases: a 63-year-old lost Rs 9.25 lakh on a share-trading app promising high returns; a fruit vendor lost Rs 1 lakh while applying for a fake Rs 3 lakh 'PayTM' loan; a youth paid Rs 1.5 lakh in fees for a fake overseas manager job. Police advise not handing phones to strangers claiming to be bank staff and verifying overseas jobs before paying fees.

title: Cyber Byte (English) July 2025
publisher: Communication & IT Directorate, Central Reserve Police Force (MHA)
notes: Reports the Uttarakhand STF arrest of the alleged mastermind of a Rs 750 crore interstate cyber fraud: a chartered accountant who set up 35-40 shell companies for Chinese operatives and extorted money through fraudulent loan apps (Inst Loan, Maxi Loan, KK Cash, RupeeGo, Lendkar and others), harassing people while posing as company representatives.

title: Gurugram police nab two in WhatsApp trading scam
notes: Gurugram Cyber Police traced Rs 25 lakh from a WhatsApp stock-trading fraud to an account whose holder had sold it for a 2% commission on money passing through; the buyer, a former private bank manager, sold his own account for 4%. Both were arrested; police said 33 bank employees had been arrested in cyber fraud cases.
